checks: Checked 05b459fea3722ebb §4, Lemma 2 and (3), and its §3 midpoint argument against the frozen statement. The frozen proof uses the accepted finite-set Helly lemma for the needed base selection.

Compactness bounds the number of nonempty integer fibers. Each fiber is compact convex and has Hausdorff dimension equal to its affine dimension. Their finite union therefore has maximum dimension q, and exactly the q-dimensional fibers have positive q-measure.

A same-parity midpoint is integral and its fiber contains the Minkowski midpoint. Holding a point of one endpoint fiber fixed gives a translate of the other scaled by one half, so the midpoint fiber has dimension at least q and belongs to P.
Two same-parity points in an empty vertex set would give a point of P in its hull that cannot be a vertex. Hence each such set has at most k points, including a singleton P.

Each E_J is convex because C and all complements are convex and projection preserves convexity. Its possibly nonclosed trace is covered by the accepted lemma. A base is outside E_J exactly when the original caps in J cover the entire actual fiber there, including boundaries.

Local covers give an empty intersection on P, so at most k lists suffice. Their union contains at most kt original indices. The argument includes dimension-zero singleton fibers and the sole base when n=0.
